description.ncbi_summary: Predicted to enable calcium channel regulator activity and neuropeptide Y receptor activity. Involved in cardiac left ventricle morphogenesis and outflow tract morphogenesis. Located in cilium. Implicated in Huntington's disease; morbid obesity; and obesity. Biomarker of peripheral artery disease and temporal lobe epilepsy. [provided by Alliance of Genome Resources, Apr 2022]

uniprot_function.text: Receptor for neuropeptide Y (NPY) and peptide YY (PYY) (PubMed:7592910, PubMed:7559383, PubMed:35507650, PubMed:36525977, PubMed:38882210). Can also bind with lower affinity pancreatic polypeptide (PP/PPY) and [Leu-31, Pro-34]NPY, an analog of NPY modified at residues 31 and 34 of the mature form. NPY or PYY binding induces adenylate cyclase-inhibiting G protein-coupled receptor signaling, resulting in inhibition of cAMP production (PubMed:7592910, PubMed:7559383, PubMed:35507650, PubMed:38882210). Receptor activation by ligands also leads to an increase of intracellular Ca(2+) levels (PubMed:7559383, PubMed:7592910). Involved in the regulation of colonic antisecretory tone, and colonic contractility (By similarity). As receptor for peptide PYY(3-36) in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus, it is involved in the down-regulation of appetite and food intake (By similarity).
